Mr Khumalo invested R10 000 into a savings account that earned simple
interest at the rate of 10% per annum. How many years did it take for the
investment to grow to R30 000?

A construction vehicle was bought exactly one year ago. At present, the book
value of this vehicle is R183 680.

1.2.1 The value of this construction vehicle depreciated annually at the rate
of 18% p.a. in the first year.
Calculate the original purchase price of the construction vehicle.

Lozze After the first year, the value of this construction vehicle will
depreciate annually at the rate of 16% p.a. on the reducing balance
method for the remaining years.

Calculate the book value of the construction vehicle exactly three
years after it was bought.

A bank charges interest on a credit card account at the rate of 23% p.a.,
compounded monthly. Convert this nominal interest rate to an effective interest
rate.

An amount of R7 500 was deposited into a savings account that earned interest
at the rate of 1% p.a., compounded quarterly. The accumulated amount in the
account was R17 752,20 at the end of 28 quarters after the initial deposit was
made.

1.4.1 How many years did it take for the accumulated amount in this
account to grow to R17 752,20 ?

1.4.2 Calculate the value of r, the quarterly rate of interest.

Three women had R10 000 each. They pooled their money together and
invested R30 000 in a stokvel account. Three years after making the initial
deposit, they withdrew R12 000 from the account. The account paid interest at
the rate of 13% p.a., compounded monthly for the first three years and changed
to 14,25% p.a., compounded half-yearly thereafter. They withdrew the total
accumulated amount 5 years after making the initial deposit.

Calculate the amount of interest each woman received at the end of 5 years.

2:2 There are 50 learners in Grade 11 at a certain school. Each of them takes part in
at least one of these three extra-mural activities: plays Piano (P), Swims (S) or
plays Cricket (C).

A survey of these 50 learners provided the following information:
e x learners play cricket only.

30 learners play piano.

24 learners swim.

16 learners swim and play piano.

9 learners swim and play cricket.

9 learners play piano and cricket, but don’t swim.

4 learners play piano, swim and play cricket.

2.2.1 Draw a Venn Diagram to represent the above information. (3)

2.2.2 Calculate the probability of randomly selecting a learner who plays

cricket only. (3)
2.2.3 Are the events playing piano and swimming independent? Show all
necessary calculations to support your answer. (4)
2:3 Sarah was given a keyholder that contains 6 keys that fit a lock. However, only

2 of these keys will open the lock. She randomly selects a key from the

keyholder and tries to open the lock. If the key does not open the lock, she

removes it from the keyholder and puts it in her pocket. She repeats the process

by randomly selecting one of the remaining keys in the keyholder.

Calculate the probability that Sarah will open the lock in her first THREE tries. (5)
